title: This Tesla owner won a $10k refund in court for Tesla’s FSD lies (Updated)
summary: A Tesla owner successfully sued Tesla in small claims court for a $10,600 refund for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) software, which failed to deliver on its promises. Despite initial delays and Tesla's attempts to push back deadlines, the court ultimately ruled in the owner's favor, citing Tesla's lack of a meritorious defense and CEO Elon Musk's admission that older hardware cars would never achieve full self-driving. This case highlights a growing trend of owners seeking refunds for undelivered FSD capabilities, with similar class-action lawsuits emerging globally.

title: Tesla Robotaxi fleet in Texas is less than one-tenth of Waymo's (TSLA:NASDAQ)
summary: Tesla's authorized robotaxi fleet in Texas has considerably fewer vehicles than Waymo's, with Tesla having 42 robotaxis compared to Waymo's significantly larger presence. This data comes from a database maintained by the state's Department of Motor Vehicles.

title: Tesla reveals its Texas robotaxi fleet is dwarfed by Waymo’s
summary: Tesla operates a robotaxi fleet of only 42 vehicles in Texas, according to recent DMV registrations, a stark contrast to rival Waymo's 577 vehicles. This count provides the most concrete assessment yet of Tesla's Texas network, which began in Austin last June and has since expanded to Dallas and Houston. Despite Elon Musk's previous ambitious projections for Tesla's robotaxi expansion, the current figures indicate a more modest start for the service, which is central to Tesla's strategy to become an AI and robotics leader.

title: SpaceX is going public - What does this mean for Tesla? for NASDAQ:TSLA by Bmillytookprof
summary: The upcoming SpaceX IPO, potentially valued at $1.75T-$2T, could significantly benefit Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) by reinforcing the perception of Elon Musk's companies as an interconnected ecosystem focused on AI, robotics, and infrastructure. This "halo effect" could drive momentum buying, expand the AI narrative for Tesla, and attract both retail and institutional inflows, potentially pushing Tesla's stock upwards. While risks like EV competition and valuation concerns exist, the IPO could solidify Wall Street's view of Musk's ventures as a unified empire, making Tesla a major beneficiary.

While some details like specific vehicle integration and cost implications are still unknown, Sensify is designed for both electric and internal combustion engine platforms and features built-in redundancies for safety.

The rebates, launched in 2024, were halted for Tesla and Chinese-made vehicles last year in retaliation for tariffs.

title: China's auto industry is unlikely to return to 'golden era,' NIO CEO says
summary: William Li, CEO of Chinese EV maker NIO, stated that China's auto industry has likely passed its "golden era" due to a prolonged downturn in domestic car sales, despite strong export performance. Li emphasized NIO's focus on its home market, highlighting that China remains the most efficient place for pure electric vehicle investments compared to overseas expansion. The company plans to significantly increase spending on computing resources for smart-driving development to navigate intensifying domestic competition in a saturated market.

title: SunCar Technology Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: SunCar Technology Group Inc. reported its first quarter 2026 financial results, achieving its third consecutive quarter of profitability with a net income of $1.6 million, an increase from a net loss in the prior year. SunCar also expanded its partnerships with major companies like Tesla, Xiaomi, and various banks and insurance providers, leveraging AI technology for enhanced services and anticipating approximately $600 million in revenue for the full year 2026.

title: Why Tesla’s Lens Cleaning Patent Matters For Optimus, Robotaxi - Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA)
summary: Tesla recently received a patent for a "Lens Cleaning System" designed for its robotaxis and Optimus humanoid robot. This system, which uses fluid and wipers, aims to keep cameras clean without human intervention, addressing debris issues for robotaxis and maintaining the Optimus's vision. The patent is crucial as Tesla shifts its focus towards robotics, AI, and self-driving technology, with Elon Musk believing these areas will drive the company's future valuation significantly.

title: Beam (BEEM) Q4 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Beam Global (BEEM) showcased a significant transformation in its revenue model for fiscal year 2025, moving away from U.S. federal government dependence towards commercial and international customers. Despite a challenging year with a decrease in overall revenue due to policy changes, the company achieved sequential revenue growth in Q4 2025, diversified its product portfolio to include smart cities and energy storage solutions, and expanded its international footprint. Beam Global emphasizes its debt-free status, access to a substantial credit facility, and strategic focus on recurring revenue streams and innovative technologies like autonomous vehicle charging and drone energy solutions for future growth.

title: Jefferies (JEF) issues autocallable buffered leveraged notes linked to worst-performing tech trio
summary: Jefferies Financial Group Inc. has priced an offering of $1.185 million in Senior Autocallable Buffered Leveraged Notes. These notes, maturing on May 28, 2031, are linked to the performance of Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), Microsoft Corporation (MSFT), and Tesla, Inc. (TSLA), specifically to the worst-performing of the trio. The notes offer a 200% participation rate on upside at maturity if the worst-performing underlying appreciates, with potential for early call on August 24, 2026, and significant principal loss risk if the worst-performing underlying declines below its threshold value.

title: Exxon wins approval to move from New Jersey to Texas
summary: Exxon Mobil shareholders have approved the company's plan to redomicile from New Jersey to Texas, despite recommendations against it from proxy advisory firms. The move is intended to align the company's legal home with its Houston headquarters and take advantage of Texas's business-friendly legal environment. Investors also rejected a proposal to expand automatic voting options for retail investors, securing another win for Exxon's board.

title: Tesla's long-awaited Roadster will be built in Texas, executives say
summary: Tesla executives have confirmed that the long-awaited Roadster, dubbed an "all-electric supercar," will be built at Gigafactory Texas, signaling further investment in the Austin-area plant. The vehicle is expected to achieve 0-60 mph in 1.9 seconds, a top speed of 250 mph, and a 620-mile range. This marks the return of the Roadster, with its second generation having faced several production delays since its initial prototype in 2006.

title: Tesla is ready to resurrect its long-awaited Roadster at Gigafactory Texas, execs say
summary: Tesla executives have confirmed that the next-generation Roadster, an all-electric supercar, will be produced at Gigafactory Texas. Chief Designer Franz von Holzhausen and engineering Vice President Lars Moravy stated that fans can expect developments in the coming months, signaling further investment in the Austin factory. This move adds a high-performance vehicle to the facility's current production of the Cybertruck, Model Y, and Cybercab, showcasing Tesla's continued expansion in Texas.

title: EV insurance up 42.5% at SunCar as Tesla expands use, banks add chauffeur deals
summary: SunCar Technology (NASDAQ: SDA) reported strong Q1 2026 financial results, achieving its third consecutive profitable quarter with revenue up 28% year-over-year to $131.2 million and net income of $1.6 million. The company saw significant growth in EV insurance premiums, surging 42.5% to $514.4 million, driven by expanded partnerships with major EV makers like Tesla and Xiaomi. SunCar also secured substantial multi-year contracts with prominent banks such as AgBank and Minsheng Bank for chauffeur and transportation services, projecting full-year 2026 revenue of approximately $600 million.

title: Michael Burry Compares OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX IPO Hype To Dot-Com Bubble
summary: Michael Burry, known for predicting the 2008 financial crisis, is comparing the immense hype surrounding upcoming IPOs for companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX to the dot-com bubble. He suggests that the current market concentration of hype and capital in AI and space tech is reaching extreme levels, similar to the speculative period of the late 1990s. Burry warns investors that while these companies are significant, their valuations might be assuming perfection, creating a risk of significant losses similar to those experienced by investors who bought into peak expectations during the dot-com era.
